params.textField: The peripheral nervous system consists of the sensory division and the motor division. Messages from the afferent portion of the peripheral nervous system travel up to the brain, informing the brain of sensations in the periphery. The efferent portion of the peripheral nervous system is the motor division, consisting of the *somatic nervous system* that controls movement and the *autonomic nervous system* that regulates vital organs. The autonomic nervous system is divided into two parts, the *sympathetic division* which uses adrenaline at the effector and the *parasympathetic division* that uses acetylcholine as its neurotransmitter. These two divisions are virtually opposite actions in most organs, and help maintain homeostasis.

params.textField: We can logically figure out what effect the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system divisions of the autonomic nervous system will have on various organs if we think about what happens in a fight or flight response versus what happens in an rest and digest response. The sympathetic division is nicknamed the *fight or flight division* that uses adrenaline, and the parasympathetic is nicknamed the *rest and digest division* that uses acetylcholine as the neurotransmitter at the effector. But we need to degrade that neurotransmitter in milliseconds, because we cannot keep sending messages to our vital organs. One of the primary ways in which we break down the neurotransmitters is by an enzyme in the synaptic cleft. Acetylcholine is degraded by *acetylcholinesterase* and adrenaline is degraded by *COMT and MAO*.
